findings.title: Error IDs zipped against nodestore values by position, but get_multi does not keep input order
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns one value per input ID, in input order. It doesn't. `get_multi` (src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:184) removes duplicate IDs, and it builds the result from the uncached IDs first, then adds the cached ones with `items.update(cache_items)` (base.py:199-205). It also drops IDs that aren't found, because `_get_bytes_multi` only returns hits. So when some events are cached, some are missing, or the replay's `error_ids` has duplicates, each error ID gets paired with a different event's title, message and timestamp. Seer then gets wrong error context and nothing reports it. Look each one up by key instead: `data = events.get(node_id)` for each `(event_id, node_id)` pair.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared with replay event timestamps (likely milliseconds)
findings.body: The merge compares `error_events[i]["timestamp"]`, the error event's `timestamp` from nodestore, against `event.get("timestamp", 0)` from the rrweb recording segments. Error event timestamps are float seconds since the epoch. rrweb event timestamps are milliseconds. If that holds here, every error timestamp is smaller than every breadcrumb timestamp, so all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb, not interleaved in time order. The log lines would also show two different timestamp scales. Please confirm the units and convert one side (for example `timestamp * 1000` for errors) before comparing.

findings.title: Assemble analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check, so requests that then get a 403/404 are also counted as assembles. Moving the record after the feature gate (or after validation) would count only real assemble requests.

findings.title: age/timestamp exclusivity uses truthiness, so 0 and a missing field both slip through
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `self.initial_data.get(...)` for truthiness. A report with `age: 0` plus a `timestamp` (or `timestamp: 0` plus an `age`) passes even though both fields are present. A report with neither field also passes, because both are `required=False`. If the goal is exactly one of the two, check `"age" in self.initial_data` inside a `validate()` method.

findings.title: `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams` returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always `true`. The query is effectively gated only by the feature flag. Drop the check, or test the specific fields it was meant to guard.

findings.title: get_environment_info makes one recommended-event lookup per issue
findings.body: Both the GitHub and GitLab merged-PR comment builders call `get_environment_info(issue)` for every issue in the list. Each call runs `issue.get_recommended_event()`, which queries the event store, so a comment with N issues makes N sequential event-store queries inside the comment task. The issue list is small, but these calls add up with no overall time limit.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while a search query is typed
findings.body: The `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` check sits inside the `.filter` that only runs after the early return at line 61 (`if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;`). So with an empty search box, which is the default state, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still show up. They only disappear once the user types something. Apply the hidden filter to `sorted` before the early return, e.g. `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`.

findings.title: Flex replacements drop align-items/gap the old styled components had
findings.body: The removed `Container` was `styled(FlexBox)`, so it had `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)` as well as `justify-content: space-between`. The new `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` (line 93) sets only `justify`. The second placeholder group (line 27, `<Flex>`) also loses the `align-items: center` and `gap` that `FlexBox` gave it. Unless the vitals and tabs are meant to realign, add `align="center" gap={space(1)}` to keep the layout the same.

findings.title: Removed FlexBox set height: 100%, which the Flex replacement does not
findings.body: The deleted `FlexBox` had `height: 100%` as well as `flex-grow: 1; flex-direction: column`. `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` keeps only the grow and direction. When the parent is not a flex container (or its height comes from a percentage), the waterfall may no longer fill its container. Please check the trace view layout, or keep `height: 100%`.

findings.title: Query options retry:false / staleTime:0 / refetchOnWindowFocus:false dropped, and environment no longer sent
findings.body: The old `useApiQuery` call set `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false`, and sent `environment: selection.environments`. The new `useQuery` call uses the client defaults and leaves out environment (the comment in useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys says it is unsupported). Was this intended? If the defaults allow retries, a failing attributes endpoint now retries before `error` is set. `isLoading` now also follows `isFetching`, so background refetches report loading too.

findings.title: Typo "the the" in story text
findings.body: "Below is the the most basic example" should read "Below is the most basic example".

findings.title: No test posts with the browser's application/reports+json content type anymore
findings.body: Before this change, `test_logs_request_data_if_option_enabled` and `test_handles_multiple_reports` posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"`. The rewritten `test_basic`, `test_handles_multiple_reports_both_specs` and the new validation tests drop that argument, so they use the test client's default JSON format. Browsers send `application/reports+json`. The endpoint handles that type with the custom `BrowserReportsJSONParser` (`src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:69`, `:82`), and after this change no test exercises that parser. If the parser or its registration breaks, the suite stays green. Keeping `content_type="application/reports+json"` in at least `test_basic` would cover the real ingestion path.

findings.title: "Project not found" may flash while the projects store is still loading
findings.body: `useProjectFromId` looks the id up in `useProjects().projects` and returns `undefined` when there is no match (`static/app/utils/useProjectFromId.tsx:8-10`). It does not tell "not loaded yet" apart from "does not exist". The new branch shows an error Alert whenever `replayRecord.project_id` is set and the project is not in the store. If the replay details page can render before the org's projects are in the store, users would briefly see a false error instead of the loading spinner. Could this branch also check `useProjects().fetching` (or whether the store is initially loaded) before showing the error?

findings.title: Breadcrumb timestamps are in seconds here, but real rrweb events use milliseconds, which hides a unit mismatch in error interleaving
findings.body: The new tests set the top-level rrweb event `timestamp` to `now.timestamp()`, which is in seconds (here at line 188 and at 254; `test_get_request_data` uses 1.5/2.0 at 290/298). Real recording events carry milliseconds at that key. The repository's own fixtures show it: `tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py:329` uses `"timestamp": 1674291701348`, and the seconds value sits in `data.payload.timestamp` (line 333). `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[i]["timestamp"]` (the event timestamp from nodestore, in seconds, read at `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:115`) against `event.get("timestamp", 0)` (line 155). With real data, every error timestamp (~1.7e9) is smaller than every breadcrumb timestamp (~1.7e12). So all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb, and the chronological interleaving these tests claim to check never happens in production. The log lines also mix units: `as_log_message` prints ms, the error line prints seconds. Nothing reports this, and Seer gets a misleading timeline. Use millisecond timestamps for breadcrumbs in these fixtures, matching real recordings. The interleaving assertion in `test_get_request_data` will then fail until the endpoint converts one side, e.g. compares against `error_timestamp * 1000`.

findings.title: Renamed class `...TopNEventsSpans` doesn't store spans
findings.body: `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans` stores error events built from messages and fingerprints, plus one `load_data("transaction")` event, through the discover/events path (lines 1264-1339). It stores no spans. The new name suggests it covers the spans dataset, and the new `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsLogs` comment (line 3087, "implemented almost exactly the same as spans") relies on that reading. Consider a name that matches what it covers, e.g. keep `OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEvents` or use `...Discover`.
